title: Libérés de cellule  (Released from the Cell)

segments.t: Sharing a cold detention cell into the early morning hours, Gabriel helps Norman confront his deepest insecurities about working with legendary director Jacques Audiard. Moved by their honesty, the sympathetic police officer makes an unexpected decision that gives Norman a second chance at his film career. Listen to the scene in French first. Don't worry about catching every word.
Il voulait que je sois dur.
Je ne peux pas, je n'ai pas assez vécu.
Il m'a dit de chercher en moi.
J'ai cherché mais il n'y avait rien.
Tu as inventé tout un genre sur Internet.
Tu as ta propre folie, ta propre violence.
Audiard veut ce qu'il y a sous la surface.
De toute façon, c'est trop tard maintenant.
Non, ce n'est pas trop tard.
Je ne l'ai pas appelé.
Tu m'as sauvé la mise!
Monsieur Sarda, suivez-moi, s'il vous plaît.
Vous êtes libre de partir.
Je vous ai entendus parler cette nuit.
Tout le monde a peur. Il doit faire ce film.
Merci beaucoup!
Je conduis? Non.
Let's walk through the overnight conversation and release step by step.
Il voulait que je sois dur.
'He wanted me to be tough.' Expressing what someone wanted you to do requires 'wanted that I be' in French, ending with 'hard' to mean 'tough'.
Je ne peux pas, je n'ai pas assez vécu.
'I cannot do it, I have not lived enough.' Notice 'enough' sits ahead of 'lived' in French—reversing English 'lived enough'—and 'I cannot' needs no 'do it'.
Il m'a dit de chercher en moi.
'He told me to search within myself.' Reporting a command uses 'told me of to-search' with 'of' as the bridge, ending with 'in me' for 'within myself' in French.
J'ai cherché mais il n'y avait rien.
'I searched but there was nothing.' Shifting 'there has' into its ongoing-past shape builds 'there was', negated with 'nothing' at the close in French.
Tu as inventé tout un genre sur Internet.
'You invented a whole genre on the Internet.' Putting 'all' ahead of 'a genre' creates a handy pattern meaning 'a whole genre' in French.
Tu as ta propre folie, ta propre violence.
'You have your own madness, your own violence.' Watch the position shift: right after 'your', the term that means 'clean' afterward instead means 'own' in French!
Audiard veut ce qu'il y a sous la surface.
'Audiard wants what lies beneath the surface.' Literally 'that which there is under the surface', that smooth relative chunk covers English 'what lies beneath'.
De toute façon, c'est trop tard maintenant.
'In any case, it is too late now.' Opening with 'of every manner' lets a speaker sigh and sum things up, capped with 'too late now' in French.
Non, ce n'est pas trop tard.
'No, it is not too late.' Wrapping 'is' cleanly inside the two negative pieces overturns Norman's despair word by word in French.
Je ne l'ai pas appelé.
'I did not call him.' Joining 'him' onto 'have' inside the negative frame keeps 'called' outside at the end in French.
Tu m'as sauvé la mise!
'You saved my skin!' Literally 'saved to-me the stake', this gambling idiom about rescuing someone's bet on the table means 'you saved my skin!' in French.
Monsieur Sarda, suivez-moi, s'il vous plaît.
'Mr. Sarda, follow me, please.' Addressing Gabriel by polite title and surname, the officer attaches 'me' onto 'follow' with a hyphen in French.
Vous êtes libre de partir.
'You are free to leave.' Related to 'liberty', the term meaning 'free' links to 'to leave' with 'of' rather than 'to' in French.
Je vous ai entendus parler cette nuit.
'I heard you talking last night.' Watch two details: 'heard' adds a silent '-s' for the two men, and 'this night' means 'last night' during the overnight hours in French.
Tout le monde a peur. Il doit faire ce film.
'Everyone has fear. He must make this movie.' Remember that feelings like fear pair with 'has' in French, and 'all the world' always takes a singular action.
Merci beaucoup!
'Thank you very much!' Warm and versatile, this two-word classic works equally well with friends, strangers, or police officers in French.
Je conduis? Non.

'Should I drive? No.' Asking 'I drive?' in the simple present is how French speakers playfully ask 'shall I drive?' when handing over keys. Now let's listen to the whole scene again at normal speed, and see how much more you catch.
Il voulait que je sois dur.
Je ne peux pas, je n'ai pas assez vécu.
Il m'a dit de chercher en moi.
J'ai cherché mais il n'y avait rien.
Tu as inventé tout un genre sur Internet.
Tu as ta propre folie, ta propre violence.
Audiard veut ce qu'il y a sous la surface.
De toute façon, c'est trop tard maintenant.
Non, ce n'est pas trop tard.
Je ne l'ai pas appelé.
Tu m'as sauvé la mise!
Monsieur Sarda, suivez-moi, s'il vous plaît.
Vous êtes libre de partir.
Je vous ai entendus parler cette nuit.
Tout le monde a peur. Il doit faire ce film.
Merci beaucoup!
Je conduis? Non.
Thanks to Gabriel's clever bluff and a compassionate police officer, Norman regains his confidence and heads toward his big-screen debut. See you next time!
À bientôt!
